Every admitted compiler branch now requires a typed capability marked admitted, while the checked JSON projection is generated from that Haxe authority and rejects stale or mutated copies.
Numeric evidence is intentionally split into exact admitted subsets; plain Float division, broad overflow, coercion, and platform-width behavior remain unverified-owned.
Strict PHP equality is justified only by the currently validated Int operands and is not generalized to dynamic or foreign values.
Source mutation and foreign/runtime/stdlib boundaries remain outside this slice and are retained as explicit unsupported or unverified capabilities.

The cross-module call now emits as two independently mapped type artifacts plus a source-derived dependency-ordered bootstrap; wordpresshx-reflaxe-php.7 owns that output-shape evidence separately from this semantic matrix.

The loop slice admits only explicit assignment to typed Int variables, Int <=, and normal pre-test while; compound assignment and do-while have source-positioned compile-negative owners with no partial output.
The small finite accumulation fixture does not establish loop termination, integer overflow, break/continue, increment/decrement, or generalized mutable storage semantics.
The array slice admits only direct Array<Int> literals and constant reads whose bounds are proven from that typed local; dynamic and out-of-bounds reads fail before publication.

Stock Haxe returned null for the out-of-bounds fixture while native PHP emitted an Undefined array key warning, so direct arbitrary PHP indexing is intentionally withheld until an owned runtime representation can preserve Haxe behavior without hidden stderr.

The first array-mutation slice emits native PHP append only for a compiler-owned Array<Int> local and an admitted Int argument in a direct statement; the updated exact length proof then protects the observed index read.
Push return values and pushes inside branches or loops have stock-Haxe-valid negative owners, so path-dependent length state and PHP array_push reference semantics cannot enter this slice.
The indexed-write slice reuses the exact receiver, constant-index, and bounds proof from reads, then emits one typed-IR native PHP assignment without changing the tracked length.

Dynamic, out-of-bounds, and branch writes have stock-Haxe-valid negative owners; aliases/references, assignment results, other mutators, iteration, ordering, mixed/null elements, nested arrays, and general collection/runtime semantics remain unsupported or unverified.

The pop slice emits one native array_pop call only for a compiler-owned, compiler-proven non-empty Array<Int> local in a direct result-discarded statement, then reduces the exact tracked length by one.

Return use, an empty receiver, control-flow mutation, and a read of the removed index have stock-Haxe-valid negative owners; PHP array_pop reference semantics cannot reach aliases because this slice admits only the owned local receiver.
The String slice accepts only operands already typed as String; a compile-negative numeric-coercion fixture prevents silently inheriting PHP coercion rules.

The UTF-8 transcript directly observes a three-byte arrow and four-byte non-BMP rocket under stock Haxe and PHP, while String length, indexing, normalization, invalid Unicode, parameters, and returns remain unverified or unsupported.

PHP strict_types is selected by the caller; therefore handwritten weak-PHP callers and public adapter ABI behavior remain outside this source-owned Haxe call claim.

The former runtime-dividend negative fixture became the positive tracer. Zero and Float remainder fixtures remain compile-negative, while runtime divisors and compound assignment stay outside the admitted claim.
Runtime dividend division reuses the compiler-owned Int32 helper and admits only Std.int over exact Int operands with a compiler-proven nonzero constant divisor.
The helper uses native intdiv for truncation toward zero, then sign-extends the low 32 bits so the Haxe minimum Int divided by -1 wraps instead of leaking PHP's wider result.
The former runtime-dividend division negative fixture became the positive tracer. Zero and Float divisors remain compile-negative, while arbitrary Std.int conversions stay outside the claim.

Distinct review found that no fixture actually protected the runtime-divisor boundary. A separate stock-Haxe-valid two-parameter division fixture now proves the custom compiler rejects that shape before output.
Exact Bool equality and inequality validate both operands recursively before emitting strict PHP === or !==, so PHP truthiness and scalar coercion cannot enter the admitted path.
A stock-Haxe-valid Bool/null comparison now fails before output. Mixed types, bitwise Bool operations, object identity, mutation, and foreign values remain outside the claim.
Exact Int inequality validates both operands recursively before emitting strict PHP !==, so PHP scalar coercion cannot enter the admitted path.
The first Int predicate adds an explicit source-owned Bool-call shape with required Int parameters. It does not weaken Bool-parameter calls or admit general predicate signatures.
A stock-Haxe-valid Float inequality fixture fails before output. Mixed numeric, null, object, coercive, and foreign comparisons remain outside the claim.
Exact non-null String inequality validates both operands recursively before emitting strict PHP !==, so PHP scalar coercion and nullable legacy-Haxe behavior cannot enter the admitted path.

The String predicate adds one source-owned Bool-call shape with required String parameters. A stock-Haxe-valid null argument fails before output, while normalization, malformed UTF-8, and foreign values remain outside the inequality claim.
Exact non-null String less-than validates and lowers each operand once, then emits strcmp(left, right) < 0. Direct PHP < is rejected because it compares numeric-looking Strings as numbers.
Distinct review added an arrow-before-rocket vector because the first UTF-8 pair differed at ASCII PHP/Reflaxe characters and did not exercise non-ASCII ordering.

A stock-Haxe-valid Null<String> ordering fixture fails before output. String <=, >, >=, locale-aware ordering, normalization, malformed UTF-8, coercion, objects, and foreign values remain outside this claim.

findings: Runtime multiplication reuses the existing Int32 helper. Every signed 32-bit product fits in the required signed 64-bit PHP intermediate, and low-bit sign extension restores the Haxe Int result.
The old runtime and overflow multiplication negative fixtures became obsolete when the same cases moved into the positive tracer. Float multiplication remains the focused negative boundary.
Runtime unary negation reuses the existing Int32 helper and preserves readable native PHP for safe constants.
The old runtime and overflow negation negative fixtures became obsolete when their cases moved into the positive tracer. Float negation remains the focused negative boundary.
Runtime signed Int dividends now use native PHP remainder only after the divisor is proven constant and nonzero. The positive tracer covers positive, negative, and minimum-Int dividends.

Runtime signed Int dividends now use the existing Int32 helper for Std.int division after the divisor is proven constant and nonzero. The positive tracer covers positive, negative, and signed-minimum overflow behavior.
Exact Bool equality and inequality now use strict PHP identity operators after both operands pass the admitted Bool validator.
Exact Int inequality now uses strict PHP !== after both operands pass the admitted Int validator. A dedicated source-owned Int predicate preserves the call boundary.
Exact non-null String inequality now uses strict PHP !== after both operands pass the admitted String validator. A dedicated source-owned String predicate preserves the call boundary.

Exact non-null String less-than now uses PHP strcmp compared with zero after both operands pass the admitted String validator. Numeric-looking and multi-byte UTF-8 vectors preserve lexical ordering without a runtime artifact.
